source.title: More Communication Does Not Result in Smaller Generalization Error in Federated Learning
source.authors: Romain Chor; Milad Sefidgaran; Abdellatif Zaidi

record.tranche_reason: Extends generalization-gap measurement to federated least-squares regression, varying communication rounds under a one-epoch training setup.
record.gate_note: The paper measures generalization error as communication rounds vary. It does not directly sweep mini-batch size; its discussion relates the R=n endpoint to SGD with mini-batch size K.
record.test_reason: The study varies communication frequency in federated least-squares regression and measures population loss minus training loss. V5 concerns batch-size effects on held-out performance in image classifiers and language models. Communication rounds do not constitute a batch-size sweep, and an increasing generalization gap does not establish worsening held-out performance when training loss also decreases. The other versions are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the numerical experiment. The authors derive a generalization-error upper bound and observe an increasing bound and measured gap with communication rounds in their experiments. Together with decreasing empirical risk, they suggest optimizing communication rounds to reduce population risk. The bound alone does not prove that the actual gap universally increases.
record.recipe_differences: Federated multi-round SGD on OLS regression; varies communication rounds rather than directly comparing batch sizes or the image and language training recipes in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured generalization error changes with the number of communication rounds R.

fits_no_version.finding: For one-epoch federated OLS on friedman1 with n=500, K=10, d=10 and learning rate 0.01, the measured population-minus-training loss gap increases with communication rounds. The authors also report decreasing empirical risk.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More frequent model averaging can increase the generalization gap in federated regression even while reducing training loss; this does not establish an increase in population loss.

record.problems: The numerical experiment uses one regression dataset for Figure 3 and reports no uncertainty estimates. The study does not directly vary batch size.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows bear on the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width effects beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected image networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance at fixed epoch budgets in image classification or language modeling, workload-dependent thresholds, and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, training-set size dependence, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against alternative measures.

record.verdict_notes: Section II-C invokes cited batch-size findings to interpret communication endpoints; these are not independent batch-size results from this study. Appendix B reports consistent regression results on california_housing without numerical details, also outside the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer tuning.

The paper measures communication rounds in federated least-squares regression, not a direct batch-size sweep on image classifiers or language models. It does not compare recipe adaptations or establish a workload-dependent batch threshold.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: OLS
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of federated communication rounds R and measured expected generalization error.
rows.measure: Expected generalization error (6), estimated experimentally using a test dataset of size Ntest = 10^3.
rows.value: The measured generalization error increases with R; precise values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper states that Figure 3 shows the measured generalization error increasing with R. No precise plotted values are stated in the text.
rows.check: The reported increasing gap with communication rounds is accurately extracted, but cannot determine V5's effect. Local updates use individual samples; only the R=n endpoint is equivalent to centralized SGD with batch size K. The outcome is a test-minus-training loss gap, rather than test loss itself.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
